objection.status: error reported by an ordinary grader
objection.quote:
Thus $V$ contains **at most one** positive number.  Consequently, either  

* (i) $g\equiv 0$ (constant), which gives $f(x)=x$, a solution; or  
* (ii) there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.
objection.witness: The dichotomy after §3 is unjustified: showing V has at most one positive element does not give V ⊆ {0,c}, since g(x)=f(x)-x may a priori be negative (only g(x)>-x is noted). The arithmetic-progression argument of §3 also assumes c1,c2>0. A short argument (g(u)=c<0 forces u+nc=f^n(u)>0 for all n, absurd) is missing.
